summary: SASSA confirmed the revised November 2026 payment dates on 14 October 2026, brought forward ahead of the Local Government Elections: Older Persons on Friday 30 October, Disability on Monday 2 November and Children's Grants on Tuesday 3 November 2026. The fourth payment day is Thursday 5 November. The SRD R370 date is announced later in the month.
content:
# SASSA Confirms Revised November 2026 Grant Payment Dates

SASSA has confirmed the revised November 2026 payment dates. Because 4 November 2026 is the Local Government Elections public holiday, the November cycle was brought forward with the approval of the National Treasury. The agency announced the revised dates in a media statement on **14 October 2026**.

## Confirmed November 2026 Dates

| Grant | November 2026 payment date |
|---|---|
| Older Persons | **Friday 30 October 2026** |
| Disability | **Monday 2 November 2026** |
| Children's Grants | **Tuesday 3 November 2026** |
| Grants under review (fourth payment day) | **Thursday 5 November 2026** |
| SRD R370 | Not yet announced — see below |

- Older Persons grants are paid first, on **Friday 30 October 2026**.
- Disability grants follow on **Monday 2 November 2026**.
- Children's Grants are paid on **Tuesday 3 November 2026**.
- The **fourth payment day, Thursday 5 November 2026**, is for beneficiaries whose grants fall within the review process — it is not a general payment day for everyone.

## The SRD R370 Date Is Still Separate

The SRD R370 grant is not part of this announcement. It is paid in batches during the **last week of the month**, and is only confirmed after mid-month. Check your own 'Pay Day' on the official SRD portal (srd.sassa.gov.za).

## What This Means for You

- **All eligible beneficiaries will still be paid** — the change is to payment *dates*, not eligibility or amounts.
- **If you receive the Older Persons grant, note that the November payment moves to 30 October 2026.**
- Confirm your personal date on the official SRD portal, by USSD, or on the SASSA WhatsApp line.

## How to Confirm Your Own Dates

- Check the official SRD status portal (srd.sassa.gov.za) — it shows your own 'Pay Day'.
- Dial the SASSA USSD short code on any phone to check your status.
- Use the SASSA WhatsApp line on 082 601 0111.
- Phone the SASSA helpline on **0800 60 10 11**.

See the [payment calendar](/payment-calendar) for every month's dates.

## How We Verified This

This is based on SASSA's official media statement dated **14 October 2026**, which confirmed the revised November dates and the reason (the 4 November Local Government Elections public holiday). The National Treasury approved the revised dates. We cross-checked the dates against reporting by SAnews/gov.za, IOL, SABC and The Citizen.

title: Foster Child Grant Rises to R1,300 a Month from October 2026
summary: The Foster Child Grant increased from R1,290 to R1,300 a month with effect from 1 October 2026, set out in Government Gazette No. 54397. It is the only SASSA grant to rise in October — every other permanent grant is unchanged until April 2027.
content:
# Foster Child Grant Rises to R1,300 a Month from October 2026

The **Foster Child Grant** increased from **R1,290 to R1,300 a month with effect from 1 October 2026**. The increase is set out in **Government Gazette No. 54397 (Government Notice R.7287, 23 March 2026)** and was confirmed in Parliament's 2026/27 social-grant budget briefing.

## What Changed

Only the Foster Child Grant amount changed in October 2026. It is the **only SASSA grant with a second increase this year** — a further R10 on top of the R40 rise in April 2026 (R1,250 → R1,290 → R1,300).

| Grant | From 1 April 2026 | From 1 October 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Foster Child Grant | R1,290 | **R1,300** |
| Older Persons (60–74) | R2,400 | R2,400 (unchanged) |
| Older Persons (75+) | R2,420 | R2,420 (unchanged) |
| Disability | R2,400 | R2,400 (unchanged) |
| Care Dependency | R2,400 | R2,400 (unchanged) |
| War Veterans | R2,420 | R2,420 (unchanged) |
| Child Support | R580 | R580 (unchanged) |
| Grant-in-Aid | R580 | R580 (unchanged) |

## Why Only the Foster Grant

The Minister of Social Development gazetted a two-stage increase for the Foster Child Grant: R1,290 from 1 April 2026 and R1,300 from 1 October 2026. The other permanent grants were increased once, in April, and are **not due for another increase until April 2027**.

## What This Means for You

- If you receive the Foster Child Grant, your **payment from October 2026 onwards is R1,300 per child** — check your own pay date, as the grant is paid in the first week of the month.
- The grant is **not means-tested**, so the increase applies to every foster child in your care under a valid children's court order.
- **Where to check:** your own payment on the SRD portal (srd.sassa.gov.za) or at a SASSA office.

## How We Verified This

This figure does **not** come from the gov.za foster-child service page, which still shows the April amount (R1,290). We used the legal instrument — the gazetted Schedule of increases — together with Parliament's budget confirmation. See the sources below.

We have updated our [Foster Child Grant guide](/grants/foster-child-grant), [grant amounts history](/guides/grant-amounts-history) and [all grants list](/grants) to reflect R1,300.

faqs.a: R1,300 a month per child, with effect from 1 October 2026. It went from R1,290 (April 2026) to R1,300 (October 2026).

faqs.a: No. The Foster Child Grant is the only SASSA grant that increased in October 2026. Older Persons, Disability, Care Dependency, War Veterans, Child Support and Grant-in-Aid amounts are unchanged since April 2026 and rise again only in April 2027.

title: SASSA Tightens Grant Controls — What the 'Integrity' Checks Mean for Your Grant
summary: On 9 October 2026 SASSA defended its grant reviews, eLife certification and biometric enrolment as integrity controls that are not designed to terminate grants arbitrarily — after the Auditor-General told Parliament the agency paid R1.33 billion to ineligible beneficiaries in 2025/26. Here is what the checks are and what to do if you are asked to verify.
content:
# SASSA Tightens Grant Controls — What the 'Integrity' Checks Mean for Your Grant

On **9 October 2026** SASSA issued a statement defending its grant controls after media reports about money paid to beneficiaries who may not have qualified during 2025/26. The agency says its reviews, eLife certification and biometric enrolment are **integrity checks — not a programme to cancel grants arbitrarily**.

## What Prompted It

The issue was raised with the **Portfolio Committee on Social Development on 7 October 2026**. SASSA acknowledged reports of payments to beneficiaries who may not have been eligible and said it is strengthening controls to protect the integrity of the social assistance system.

## What the Checks Actually Are

SASSA listed its main controls:

- **Grant reviews / reassessments** — periodic checks that you still qualify (see our [grant verification guide](/guides/grant-verification-process) and [review reassessment guide](/guides/sassa-grant-renewal)).
- **eLife certification** — the annual proof-of-life check for beneficiaries paid through a bank, institution or procurator (see [life certification](/guides/life-certification)).
- **Beneficiary biometric enrolment** — capturing fingerprints as an identity check (see [biometric fixes](/guides/biometric-fix-guide)).

SASSA stressed these are **controls to verify identity and eligibility** — they are **not designed to arbitrarily terminate grants**. A review does not automatically mean your grant is cancelled.

## What the Auditor-General Found

The Portfolio Committee on Social Development was briefed on the Auditor-General's 2025/26 findings in early October 2026. According to the AGSA presentation:

- SASSA paid about **R1.33 billion** to ineligible beneficiaries in 2025/26, down from about **R2.3 billion** in 2024/25.
- **R211 million** went to people who had died (up from R18.6 million the year before).
- **R266.8 million** went to government employees earning above the threshold.
- **R18.9 million** went to people with invalid ID documents, and **R235.1 million** to people on the GEPF.
- **R604.3 million** was paid despite an incomplete database (down from R1.776 billion).

SASSA's 9 October 2026 statement was its response to these reports. The agency said the reviews, eLife certification and biometric enrolment exist to prevent exactly these payments, and that beneficiaries who genuinely qualify have nothing to fear.

## What the Review Numbers Show (2026/27)

- About **352,000** beneficiaries are targeted for review in 2026/27.
- **169,049** beneficiaries did not respond to a review notice in 2025/26 and their grants lapsed, were cancelled or terminated — but **31,759** later presented and had their grants restored.
- Beneficiaries have **90 days** to present themselves for a review.
- SASSA has said reviews will **pause temporarily in November and December 2026**.

## What to Do If You're Asked to Verify

1. **Respond to the notice** — a review usually needs documents or a biometric/eLife step.
2. **Make sure your cellphone number is RICA'd in your own name** so you receive notifications (see our [phone-number guide](/guides/lost-phone-number)).
3. **Use official channels only.** SASSA will never ask you to pay to be verified.
4. **Still unsure?** Phone the SASSA helpline on **0800 60 10 11**.

The spokesperson on the statement is SASSA's **Dr Paseka Letsatsi** (082 883 9969).

faqs.q: Is SASSA cancelling grants to save money?
faqs.a: SASSA says no. It describes its reviews, eLife certification and biometric enrolment as integrity controls to confirm identity and eligibility, not a programme to arbitrarily terminate grants. A review does not automatically mean your grant is cancelled.

faqs.q: What should I do if SASSA asks me to verify my grant?
faqs.a: Respond to the notice with the requested documents or biometric/eLife step, make sure the cellphone number SASSA has is RICA'd in your own name, and use only official SASSA channels — SASSA never asks you to pay to be verified.

faqs.q: When did SASSA make this statement?
faqs.a: 9 October 2026. The issue was raised with the Portfolio Committee on Social Development on 7 October 2026.

faqs.q: How much did SASSA pay to ineligible beneficiaries?
faqs.a: The Auditor-General told Parliament that SASSA paid about R1.33 billion to ineligible beneficiaries in 2025/26, down from about R2.3 billion in 2024/25. This included R211 million to deceased beneficiaries and R266.8 million to government employees earning above the threshold.

faqs.q: How long do I have to respond to a SASSA review notice?
faqs.a: SASSA allows up to 90 days from the date of the notice: an initial 30 days to submit the requested information, and a further 60 days before the grant may be suspended (Parliamentary reply NW4444, 17 September 2026). If you do not respond, the grant is suspended — you then have 30 days from the suspension to apply for restoration before it can be lapsed. It can still be restored if you present later and still qualify.

title: SASSA Urges Beneficiaries to Stop Changing Payment Details So Often
summary: On 7 October 2026 SASSA warned that frequent changes to your payment method or bank details can delay your grant and even get it returned — especially when made close to your payment date. How to change safely.
content:
# SASSA Urges Beneficiaries to Stop Changing Payment Details So Often

On **7 October 2026** SASSA warned beneficiaries against **unnecessary and frequent changes to their payment method or bank details**, saying it can cause delays and even return a payment.

## Why It Matters

- Every change must be **verified before your next payment is processed**.
- If you change details **close to your payment date**, the change may not be processed in time and your payment can be **rejected or returned**.
- **Wrong or unactivated bank accounts** are a common cause of failed payments.

## When Changing Is Fine

Change your payment method when it genuinely needs to change — for example a new bank account, a lost card, or switching between bank transfer, Postbank or cash send. Just do it **well before your payment week**, not during it.

## How to Avoid a Rejected Payment

1. **Make changes early** — ideally at least a few weeks before your next pay date.
2. **Double-check the account number and branch code** are correct and that the account is **active and in your own name**.
3. **Confirm the change was captured** on the SRD portal (srd.sassa.gov.za) or with a SASSA official.
4. **Don't switch repeatedly** between methods in the same cycle.
5. If a payment is already missing, work through our [missing payment guide](/guides/missing-grant-payment-guide) or phone the SASSA helpline on **0800 60 10 11**.

See our guides on [payment methods](/guides/sassa-payment-methods), [opening a bank account](/guides/how-to-open-bank-account-sassa-payments) and fixing [pending bank details](/guides/bank-details-pending-fix).

faqs.q: How often can I change my SASSA payment method?
faqs.a: There is no limit in law, but SASSA advises against unnecessary and frequent changes because each change must be verified and can delay your payment. Change only when you need to, and well before your payment week.

faqs.q: Why was my SASSA payment rejected after I changed my bank details?
faqs.a: If you change your details close to your payment date, the change may not be processed in time. Wrong or unactivated account numbers also cause rejected or returned payments. Make changes early and double-check the account is active and in your own name.

faqs.q: What did SASSA say on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: SASSA urged beneficiaries to avoid unnecessary and frequent changes to their payment method, warning that changes made close to processing dates can cause delays, rejected payments or returned payments.

title: SASSA Expands Digital Services: WhatsApp Channels, Office Kiosks and Free Wi-Fi

# SASSA Expands Digital Services: WhatsApp Channels, Office Kiosks and Free Wi-Fi

On 17 September 2026 SASSA outlined its digital-services expansion at a media briefing in the Eastern Cape. The agency is adding WhatsApp support, self-service kiosks and free Wi-Fi at its offices so that more beneficiaries can handle grant enquiries without standing in a queue.

## What SASSA Announced

- **WhatsApp channels** for Social Relief of Distress (SRD) and social grant enquiries, plus a separate channel for checking review statuses. This sits alongside the self-service WhatsApp line launched in August 2026 (082 601 0111).
- **Self-service kiosks** at SASSA offices, with more advanced kiosks planned for strategic locations across the country by the 2027/28 financial year.
- **Free Wi-Fi** at SASSA offices so beneficiaries who own smartphones but have little or no data can use the online application system and the SASSA WhatsApp platform while on site.
- **A mobile app** is in development.

SASSA CEO Themba Matlou said the agency wants to build a modern organisation whose services are 'accessible, secure and citizen-centred'. SASSA stressed that the digital options work alongside face-to-face service rather than replacing it, so no beneficiary who prefers to be helped in person is left behind.

## What to Do Now

The rollout is not yet available at every office. Before travelling, confirm which services your nearest branch actually offers, and make sure SASSA has your correct cellphone number so you receive notifications.

- If your number changed, update it on the SRD portal (srd.sassa.gov.za) - our [phone-number guide](/guides/lost-phone-number) explains how.
- For review status, use the [WhatsApp self-service](/guides/sassa-whatsapp) review option.

title: SRD Grant Court Case: SCA Hears the Appeal, Judgment Reserved
summary: The Supreme Court of Appeal heard the state's appeal against the High Court rulings on the SRD R370 grant on 25 August 2026 and reserved judgment. What the courts are deciding, and why nothing changes for your grant yet.
content:
# SRD Grant Court Case: SCA Hears the Appeal, Judgment Reserved

On 25 August 2026 the Supreme Court of Appeal (SCA) in Bloemfontein heard the government's appeal against the January 2025 Gauteng High Court judgment on the SRD R370 grant. Judgment was reserved. This page explains what the courts are deciding and what it means for your grant right now.

## What the High Court Found (January 2025)

Judge Leonard Twala ruled that the SRD system was unlawfully designed and excluded millions of eligible applicants. The judgment found:

- the **online-only application** system was unconstitutional, and ordered that in-person applications be allowed
- the **R624 income threshold** was unconstitutional, and ordered it raised in line with the cost of living
- the **R370 amount** was unconstitutional, and ordered progressive increases
- **once-off payments and gifts** should not be counted as income

The government appealed against the judgment, which is why the case reached the SCA.

## What Happened at the SCA (25 August 2026)

The state - SASSA, the Department of Social Development and the National Treasury - defended the existing system. The Treasury told the court that expanding the grant could cost between about R93.5 billion and R139 billion a year and that the extra spending was unaffordable.

The judges pressed the state on whether an online-only system unfairly excludes people who cannot afford a phone or data or lack digital skills. The state argued it had added free call centres, self-service kiosks, email assistance and community outreach. Advocate Jason Brickhill, representing the applicants, told the court there are about one million SRD appeals a month - around 12 million a year - and that 99% are refused, which he called a massive red flag.

The SCA reserved judgment and asked for additional affidavits. There is no set date for the written ruling.

## What This Means for Your Grant Today

Nothing changes until the SCA rules and any order is implemented. The grant remains R370 for people who qualify, the income limit stays R624, and the online portal remains the application channel. Ignore any claim that the amount or threshold has already changed because of the case - that has not happened.

- Your amount today: R370. See [how much the SRD grant is](/how-much-is-srd-grant).
- Declined and want to challenge it now? [Read how to appeal](/guides/appeal-guide).
- The grant's history: [amounts from 2020 to 2026](/guides/grant-amounts-history).

## Sources

- [GroundUp - Judges grill Treasury on SRD grant](https://groundup.news/article/expanding-the-srd-grant-could-cost-r139-billion-a-year-national-treasury-says/)

title: SASSA Grant Suspensions During 2026 Integrity Checks – What You Need to Do
summary: SASSA suspended some SRD R370 grants during its 2026 integrity checks, aimed at reducing fraud and payment errors. Here is what to do if yours was suspended.
content:
# SASSA Grant Suspensions During 2026 Integrity Checks – What You Need to Do

SASSA has been rolling out data-integrity checks to reduce fraud and payment errors. While the goal is to eliminate fraud, some social relief of distress grants have been suspended where data mismatches were found.

## Why Were Grants Suspended?
The suspensions are driven by data mismatches identified during automated cross-checks with other government databases. The system now links your application directly with:
*   **Department of Home Affairs:** To verify identity and citizenship status.
*   **SARS (Revenue Service):** To check for undeclared income that exceeds the R624 threshold.
*   **PASA (Payments Association):** To verify that bank accounts are active and registered in the applicant's name.

## How to Check if You Are Affected
If you haven't received your February payment, your status might be 'Suspended' or 'Declined' due to 'Referred' status. 
1.  Visit the [official SRD portal](https://srd.sassa.gov.za).
2.  Check for messages such as "Identity Verification Failed" or "Alternative Income Source."
3.  If you believe this is an error, you must lodge an appeal immediately.

### Resolving the Suspension
If your grant was suspended due to unverified banking details, you must log in to the portal and re-submit your banking information. Ensure the account is a personal account and not a business or friend's account.

*   **Step 4:** Submit. SASSA will send an SMS to your registered number to confirm the change.

### Important Warning
SASSA will **never** ask for your Bank PIN or Password. Do not share your login details with anyone claiming to be a SASSA official on social media or WhatsApp.

|---|---|

   - Shoprite
   - Checkers
   - Usave
   - Pick n Pay
   - Boxer
   - Spar

title: Stokvel Payouts Triggering SRD Declines: How to Appeal and Get Your R370 Back
summary: Many SRD applicants are declined because stokvel payouts and e-wallet transfers are counted as income. SASSA's system cannot distinguish between savings and salary.
content:
# Stokvel Payouts Triggering SRD Declines: How to Appeal and Get Your R370 Back

Many SRD R370 applicants are declined for 'Income Source Detected' — not because they have a job, but because stokvel payouts and e-wallet transfers pushed their bank deposits over the R624 threshold.

## Why This Happens
SASSA's automated means test scans your bank accounts every month. The system counts **every deposit** as income — including stokvel savings payouts, family e-wallet transfers, and even refunds. If your total monthly deposits exceed R624, you are automatically declined for that month.

## Real Example
A beneficiary contributed R500/month to a stokvel for 11 months. In month 12, the stokvel paid out R5,500. SASSA saw R5,500 in deposits and declined the application — even though the money was the beneficiary's own savings being returned.

## How to Appeal
If your SRD was declined due to a stokvel payout or e-wallet transfer:
1. Log into the [ITSAA appeals portal](https://srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za) — our [appeal timeline guide](/guides/appeal-timeline) explains the full process.
2. Select 'Income Source Detected' as the reason.
3. Explain clearly: 'This was a stokvel savings payout, not income.' Provide specific dates and amounts.
4. Submit bank statements showing the transaction.

## How to Prevent Future Declines
The safest approach is to **separate your SRD income**. Open a dedicated bank account that only receives your R370 grant. Use a different account for stokvel and family transactions. See our detailed guide on [stokvel payouts and e-wallet declines](/guides/stokvel-e-wallet) for more prevention strategies.

### What If Your Appeal Is Approved?
If the Independent Tribunal (ITSAA) approves your appeal, SASSA will pay back pay for the declined month. See [how long appeals take](/guides/appeal-timeline) — typically 60 to 90 days.

# Income Source Detected: The #1 Reason SRD Grants Are Declined — Complete Fix Guide

If your SRD R370 application shows **'Declined'** with the reason 'Income Source Detected', you are not alone. It is one of the most common decline reasons for SRD applicants.

## What Triggers This Decline?
SASSA's automated system scans your bank accounts every month. It looks at **all deposits** — not just salary. The following can trigger a decline:
- A family member sending you money via **e-wallet or bank transfer**
- A **stokvel payout** being deposited into your account
- A **refund** from a store or service provider
- Someone **using your bank account** for their transactions
- Any deposit that pushes your monthly total **over R624**

The system cannot distinguish between a salary and a once-off gift — any deposit over R624 is treated as income.

## How to Fix It: Step by Step

### Step 1: Identify What Triggered It
Log into the [SRD portal](https://srd.sassa.gov.za) and review your bank statements for the declined month. Look for every deposit, no matter how small.

### Step 2: Submit an Appeal
Go to the [ITSAA appeals portal](https://srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za). Select the declined month and choose 'Income Source Detected'. Write a clear explanation of what each deposit was. Be specific with dates and amounts.

### Step 3: Provide Evidence
Upload your bank statements. If a family member sent you money, include a signed affidavit from them confirming it was a gift, not income.

### Step 4: Prevent Future Declines
The only way to avoid this is to **isolate your SRD income**. Open a separate bank account that only receives your R370 grant. Do not give this account number to anyone.

We have created in-depth guides for every aspect of this issue:

# SASSA SRD Decline Reasons 2026: Complete Guide to All 8 Decline Codes & How to Fix Each One

Many SRD R370 applications are declined each month. If yours was declined, you are not alone — and in most cases, the decline can be fixed through an appeal.

This guide explains **every SASSA SRD decline reason**, how to check which one applies to you, what to do about each one, and how to prevent future declines.

## How to Check Your Decline Reason

Before you can fix a decline, you need to know the exact reason. Here is how:

1. Go to [srd.sassa.gov.za](https://srd.sassa.gov.za)
2. Enter your **13-digit South African ID number**
3. Enter the **cellphone number** you used when applying
4. Click Submit
5. Your current status will appear. If declined, the reason will be displayed (e.g., 'Income Source Detected', 'Identity Verification Failed')

You can also check via [WhatsApp](/guides/sassa-whatsapp) (082 601 0111) or the [Moya App](/guides/moya-app-sassa) if the website is down.

## The 8 Decline Reasons

### 1. Income Source Detected

**What it means:** SASSA\'s automated system scanned your bank account and found total deposits exceeding R624 in a calendar month. This includes not just salary but also family gifts, stokvel payouts, e-wallet transfers, and even refunds.

**How to fix it:** Submit an appeal on the [ITSAA portal](https://srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za). Select 'Income Source Detected' as the reason. Explain clearly: 'This was not income — it was a [family gift/stokvel payout/refund].' Provide bank statements showing the transaction. If the deposit was from a stokvel, get a letter from your stokvel group explaining it was savings, not income.

**Prevention:** Use a separate bank account that receives ONLY your SRD grant. Ask family to send you cash instead of bank transfers.

**Related guide:** [Income Source Detected — Full Appeal Guide](/decline-reason/income-source-detected)

### 2. Identity Verification Failed (a very common decline reason)

**What it means:** The name or ID number on your SASSA application does not match the Department of Home Affairs database. Common causes: using a nickname, omitting a middle name, a typo in your ID number, or your surname has changed but SASSA still has your old surname.

**How to fix it:** Log into the SRD portal and use the 'Request Names and Surname Update' tool. Enter your details exactly as they appear on your ID document. If the online tool does not work, visit a SASSA office with your ID document and ask them to correct your name in the system.

**Prevention:** When applying, enter your name EXACTLY as it appears on your green ID book or Smart ID card.

**Related guide:** [Identity Verification Failed — Full Appeal Guide](/decline-reason/identity-verification-failed)

### 3. UIF Registered (a common decline reason)

**What it means:** Your ID number is still linked to an active UIF record from a previous employer. Even if you are no longer receiving UIF payments, an old 'registered' status is enough to trigger a decline.

**How to fix it:** Visit your nearest Department of Employment and Labour office and request a UIF clearance letter showing your status is 'Inactive' or 'Closed'. Upload this letter with your appeal on the ITSAA portal.

**Prevention:** If you leave a job, ensure your employer closes your UIF record. Keep the closure letter for your records.

**Related guide:** [UIF Registered — Full Appeal Guide](/decline-reason/uif-registered)

### 4. NSFAS Registered (common among former NSFAS students)

**What it means:** Your ID is linked to an active NSFAS record. This affects former students whose NSFAS records were never updated to 'Completed' or 'Inactive'.

**How to fix it:** Contact NSFAS directly at [www.nsfas.org.za](https://www.nsfas.org.za) or call 0800 067 327 and ask them to update your status to 'Non-Student' or 'Completed'. Once done, submit an appeal explaining that you are no longer a student.

**Prevention:** When you finish your studies, confirm with NSFAS that your record has been updated to 'Completed'.

**Related guide:** [NSFAS Registered — Full Appeal Guide](/decline-reason/nsfas-registered)

### 5. Existing SASSA Grant (occurs when you already receive a grant)

**What it means:** You are already receiving another SASSA grant. You cannot receive the SRD while also receiving Old Age, Disability, Child Support, or any other permanent grant.

**How to fix it:** You cannot appeal this decline — it is correct. If you believe the record is an error, visit a SASSA office to report fraudulent use of your ID.

**Related guide:** [Existing SASSA Grant — Full Appeal Guide](/decline-reason/existing-sassa-grant)

### 6. Government Payroll (common if you recently worked)

**What it means:** Your ID is registered on the Government Personnel Management System (PERSAL), indicating you are a government employee — even if you no longer work for government.

**How to fix it:** Contact your former government department and request a PERSAL clearance letter confirming you are no longer employed. Submit this with your appeal.

**Related guide:** [Government Payroll — Full Appeal Guide](/decline-reason/government-payroll)

### 7. Age Outside Range (less common, but easy to fix)

**What it means:** You are either under 18 or over 59. The SRD grant is for applicants aged 18 to 59.

**How to fix it:** If your age is within range but the system is wrong, submit your ID document as proof with your appeal. If you are genuinely outside the age range, apply for the appropriate grant instead.

**Related guide:** [Age Outside Range — Full Appeal Guide](/decline-reason/age-outside-range)

### 8. Deceased DHA Record (rare, but it must be resolved)

**What it means:** The Department of Home Affairs database has your ID number marked as deceased — possibly due to identity theft or an administrative error.

**How to fix it:** Visit your nearest Department of Home Affairs office with your ID document. Ask them to investigate and correct your status. If it is identity theft, open a case at the police station.

**Related guide:** [Deceased DHA Record — Full Appeal Guide](/decline-reason/deceased-dha-record)

## Step-by-Step Appeal Process

1. Go to the [ITSAA appeals portal](https://srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za)
2. Select the month you were declined
3. Choose the decline reason from the list
4. Write a clear explanation and upload any supporting documents
5. Submit and note your reference number
6. Wait 60 to 90 days for a decision

## How to Prevent Declines in Future Months

- **Use one bank account only** and keep deposits under R624 per month
- **Do not share your bank account** with family or friends
- **Keep your SASSA registered phone number active** — you need it for OTPs and verification links
- **Complete any biometric verification** within 72 hours if prompted
- **Check your status after the 15th** of each month so you can appeal quickly if declined

title: SASSA SRD R370 vs Child Support Grant 2026: Which One Should You Apply For?

# SASSA SRD R370 vs Child Support Grant 2026: Which One Should You Apply For?

If you are an unemployed caregiver with children, you may qualify for both the **SRD R370 grant** and the **Child Support Grant (CSG)**. But you can only receive one grant at a time. Which one should you choose?

This guide compares both grants side by side so you can make the right decision.

## Quick Comparison Table

| Feature | SRD R370 Grant | Child Support Grant |
|---------|---------------|-------------------|
| **Monthly Amount** | R370 | R580 per child |
| **Age Limit** | 18 to 59 years | 18+ (as caregiver) |
| **Child Age** | N/A | Under 18 |
| **Income Threshold** | R624/month | R5,800/month (single) |
| **Application** | Online only | At SASSA office |
| **Reassessment** | Every month | Every 6-12 months |
| **Asset Test** | No | No |
| **Medical Required** | No | No |

## Which Grant Pays More?

If you have **one child**, the Child Support Grant pays **R580** compared to SRD's **R370** — that is R210 more per month. If you have **two children**, the CSG pays **R1,160** — over three times the SRD amount. The CSG also has a much higher income threshold (R5,800 vs R624), meaning more people qualify.

**Verdict:** If you have at least one child under 18, the Child Support Grant is almost always the better option.

## When Should You Choose the SRD Instead?

There are a few situations where the SRD is the better choice:
- **You are not the primary caregiver** of a child (the CSG requires you to be the main person caring for the child)
- **Your income is between R624 and R5,800** — you earn too much for SRD but qualify for CSG
- **You need money immediately** — SRD is processed faster (7-30 days vs 30-90 days for CSG)
- **You cannot visit a SASSA office** — SRD is fully online

## Can You Switch Between Grants?

Yes — but not simultaneously. If you are receiving SRD and qualify for CSG, you must:
1. Apply for the Child Support Grant at a SASSA office
2. Once the CSG is approved, SRD payments will stop automatically
3. You cannot receive both in the same month

If your CSG is later cancelled (e.g., your child turns 18), you can reapply for the SRD.

## Key Differences in Application Process

The SRD grant takes **7 to 30 days** and is done entirely online at [srd.sassa.gov.za](https://srd.sassa.gov.za). You only need your ID number and phone number.

The Child Support Grant takes **30 to 90 days** and requires a visit to a SASSA office. You need your ID, the child's birth certificate, proof of income, and proof of residence. The CSG requires a means test but has a much higher income threshold.

## Decision Flowchart
1. Do you have a child under 18 living with you? Yes → Apply for CSG (it pays more). No → Apply for SRD.
2. Are you the child's primary caregiver? Yes → CSG is best. No → You may only qualify for SRD.
3. Is your income under R5,800/month? Yes → You likely qualify for CSG. No → Check if you qualify for SRD (under R624).
4. Cannot visit a SASSA office? Yes → SRD is your only option (fully online).

## Recommended Action
Apply for the **Child Support Grant first**. It pays nearly double the SRD (R580 vs R370 per child) and has a much more generous income threshold. If your CSG application is denied or takes too long, apply for the SRD as a backup while waiting.

SASSA has launched a dedicated **24/7 WhatsApp self-service channel** for COVID-19 SRD beneficiaries. Check your status, get payment dates, and access information without calling the helpline or visiting an office.

# SASSA Dismisses 14 Eastern Cape Officials for Fraud and Corruption

SASSA has dismissed **14 officials in the Eastern Cape** for fraud, corruption and related misconduct, and **11 more officials are facing disciplinary hearings**. The dismissals are part of a wider national crackdown: SASSA dismissed **43 officials for fraud and corruption in the 2025/26 financial year**, according to its report to Parliament's Standing Committee on Appropriations.

## What the Officials Are Accused Of

The cases involve allegations of:

* Fraudulent approval of social grants
* Unlawful changes to beneficiaries' banking details
* Other irregular grant administration practices

The misconduct was uncovered at SASSA offices including Komani, Mdantsane, Dutywa, eMaxesibeni (Mount Ayliff), Duncan Village, Zwide and Qonce. SASSA says it has suffered **over R3 million in losses** because of fraudulent grant administration and payment processes. It has applied for **preservation orders** to recover the public funds, and all the cases have been referred to SAPS for criminal investigation.

## Policing Itself: What This Means for Beneficiaries

The crackdown is a strong signal that SASSA is taking internal fraud seriously. It is also a reminder that **no SASSA official will ever ask for your PIN, OTP or card details** — anyone who does is a scammer.

* Unauthorised changes to banking details are exactly the kind of fraud being prosecuted. If someone claims they can 'help' you change your banking details, be suspicious.
* If a caller, SMS or app asks for your PIN or one-time PIN, report it to the SASSA fraud hotline on **0800 60 10 11**.
* See our [Scam Alert page](/scam-alert) for the warning signs and how to report fraud.
* If you are struggling with a SASSA issue, check our [Common Problems guide](/common-problems) before paying anyone for help.

# SASSA SRD R370 Payment Dates for October 2026: 22 and 23 October Confirmed

SASSA has confirmed the **October 2026 SRD R370 payment dates** as **Thursday 22 and Friday 23 October 2026**. The SRD grant is paid in batches, so you are paid on **one** of those two dates - the one shown as your personal **"Pay Day"** on the official SRD status portal - not on both.

The permanent grants were paid earlier in the month. Older Persons Grants were paid on Friday 2 October, Disability Grants on Monday 5 October, and Children's Grants on Tuesday 6 October 2026.

## October 2026 Payment Dates at a Glance

| Grant Type | Payment Date | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Older Persons Grant** | Friday, 2 October 2026 | Paid |
| **Disability Grant** | Monday, 5 October 2026 | Paid |
| **Children's Grants** | Tuesday, 6 October 2026 | Paid |
| **SRD R370 Grant** | Thursday 22 or Friday 23 October 2026 | Confirmed |
| **Grants Under Review (fourth payment day)** | Not yet confirmed | TBC |

## Why the SRD Has Two Payment Dates

The SRD grant is paid to millions of beneficiaries every month, so SASSA releases the money in batches rather than all at once. That is why there are two payment dates in October 2026.

Your **"Pay Day"** on the SRD portal tells you which batch you are in. If your Pay Day is 22 October, you do not need to check again on 23 October. If your Pay Day is 23 October, your payment is not late on the 22nd - it simply has not been released yet.

After your Pay Day, the money can take up to **48 business hours** to reflect in your bank account, depending on your bank. It is also safe to leave the money in your account - you do not need to withdraw everything on the first day.

## Check Your Own Pay Day Before You Do Anything Else

A general payment date is not a promise that your money is already in your account. Always check your own status first:

1. Go to the official SRD portal at [srd.sassa.gov.za](https://srd.sassa.gov.za).
2. Enter your 13-digit ID number and the cellphone number you used for your application.
3. Look for your **"Pay Day"** date and your payment status.
4. If your status shows **"Approved"** with a Pay Day, your payment is being processed for that date.

You can also use our [status check page](/status-check) and the [status explorer tool](/tools/status-explorer) to understand what each status message means. Only the official SRD portal can confirm your personal payment date.

## If Your Payment Has Not Arrived

If your Pay Day has passed and the money is not in your account:

- **Wait up to 48 business hours** after your Pay Day. Bank processing times differ.
- **Check your banking details.** The account must be in **your own name** and must match the ID number SASSA has on record.
- **Check your status again** on the SRD portal to confirm the payment was released and not returned.
- **Follow the missing payment steps** in our [missing grant payment guide](/guides/missing-grant-payment-guide).
- If the problem continues, contact SASSA on **0800 60 10 11**.

## Banking Details Must Be in Your Own Name

SASSA pays the SRD grant into a bank account that is registered in your own name. If you used a family member's account, a friend's account, or a funeral scheme account, the payment can fail or show as "bank details pending".

You can update your banking details on the official SRD portal. If your payment is stuck because of banking details, read our guide on [fixing bank details that are pending](/guides/bank-details-pending-fix). Never pay anyone to "fix" your banking details for you.

## The SRD Grant Has Been Extended to 31 March 2027

The SRD R370 grant has been **extended until 31 March 2027**. You do not need to reapply only because of the extension, but the grant is still reassessed **every month**. That means your approval can change from one month to the next if your bank deposits, UIF, SARS, NSFAS or Home Affairs records change.

If you were approved last month and declined this month, check the decline reason on the portal and appeal within **90 days** if it is wrong. Our [SRD grant guide](/grants/srd-r370-grant) explains approval, declines, appeals and reapplications in detail.

## Watch Out for Fake Payment Messages

Scam messages increase around payment dates. Be careful of WhatsApp messages, SMSes and social media posts that:

- claim SASSA has "released" your payment for a fee;
- ask for your PIN, OTP or bank card details;
- send a link that is not **srd.sassa.gov.za**;
- promise to move you to the front of the queue.

SASSA never asks you to pay to release a grant, and never asks for your PIN or OTP. Read our [scam alert guide](/scam-alert) and report suspicious messages.

## What to Do Next

- [Check your SRD status](/status-check) and confirm your personal Pay Day.
- See the [October 2026 payment schedule](/dates/october-2026) and the [payment calendar](/payment-calendar) for all confirmed dates.
- Read the [full SRD R370 grant guide](/grants/srd-r370-grant) for approval, banking and appeal help.
- Start again from the [SASSA Help Hub home page](/) if you are looking for a different grant.

SASSA is expected to announce the next SRD dates after mid-November 2026. Until then, treat any November SRD date you see online as unconfirmed unless SASSA has published it.
